subject.title: fix: handle Claude CLI synthetic placeholders

question: When a reused Claude live session emits a known synthetic empty result before later same-process output, should OpenClaw keep reading that process, restrict placeholder fallback to proven-terminal modes, or intentionally abandon the turn and fall back?
rationale: The same dependency event shape represents both terminal no-output metadata and an observed intermediate live-session event, so safe completion and timeout semantics require an explicit owner decision rather than a parser-only assumption.

options.title: Wait for the real live result
options.body: Treat the first known synthetic result in a reused live session as intermediate under a bounded timeout and complete only on the later real result or proven terminal exhaustion.

options.title: Limit fallback to terminal modes
options.body: Keep the marker and classifier for one-shot or otherwise proven-terminal output while leaving persistent live sessions unchanged until a separate lifecycle fix lands.

options.title: Accept immediate fallback
options.body: Land the current semantics and explicitly accept that the original live process may continue after OpenClaw abandons its answer and routes elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Wait for the real live result
recommendation.body: Treat the first known synthetic result in a reused live session as intermediate under a bounded timeout and complete only on the later real result or proven terminal exhaustion.
